lines.en: An emergency arrest by the Enforcement Division.
According to ‘Ways of Survival’, such emergency arrests were made only when a dokkaebi committed an act that seriously violated a scenario’s probability.

[Intermediate dokkaebi Paul. From this moment, you will be placed in the custody of the ‘Enforcement Division’. You may exercise your right to remain silent regarding the scenarios under your jurisdiction, and you will be stripped of all authority to conduct main scenarios.]
As the cold, mechanical recital continued, intermediate dokkaebi Paul’s expression changed from moment to moment.
[You will lose all scenario achievement points you have accumulated and be demoted to a ‘lower-grade dokkaebi’. Furthermore, as punishment for your offenses······.]
[D-demoted? Wait! Please, wait a moment!]
Intermediate dokkaebi Paul hurriedly interrupted.
He swept an aggrieved gaze over me and the surrounding dokkaebis, then shouted.
[What do you mean, suddenly ‘demoting’ me? Shouldn’t you at least tell me what I’ve done wrong?]
[Are you asking because you genuinely don’t know?]
The other dokkaebi from the Enforcement Division asked. Paul briefly faltered before that imposing presence, but spoke up again.
[I don’t know. What exactly is the problem?]
Apparently, he had even decided to brazen it out.
[Look at the constellations. Aren’t they all enjoying themselves? I believe I brought the scenario to an excellent conclusion.]
At Paul’s confident words, the dokkaebi executor frowned.
[There is no problem with probability. I obtained the constellations’ consent before initiating forced execution of the scenario, and as I said, the constellations also······.]
[······This is the problem with you streamer bastards. Always going on about those damn constellations.]
Not all dokkaebis respected ‘constellations’.
That was because some of the dokkaebis in the ‘Enforcement Division’ had once been ‘constellations’ themselves.
Beings who had been constellations, but had lost their Status through unavoidable circumstances and had no choice but to live as dokkaebis. Those were the dokkaebis of the Enforcement Division.
Perhaps feeling that his customers had been insulted, Paul held his head high.
[You go too far.]
[Don’t get smart with us, Paul.]
[Even from an executor, I cannot tolerate insults directed at my customers.]
Perhaps thinking he had gained the upper hand, Paul continued.
[I have some idea why you executors have come. Presumably, it is because I used the ‘Authority for Forced Scenario Execution’.]
[The ‘Authority for Forced Scenario Execution’ can be used only when the constellations share the burden of the scenario’s probability.]
[I know that too. Otherwise, there is a risk of probability backlash. But as long as the constellations’ satisfaction is high enough, that aspect······.]
[Satisfaction? Paul, take a look at yourself before you speak.]
At those words, Paul looked down at himself.
Bzzzzzt.
His face pale, Paul raised his head.
[Wh-what is this······?]
Blue sparks rippling through the space around him.
They were a precursor to probability backlash.
[Why is there probability backlash······?]
Probability backlash was punishment for defying the flow.
The world’s probability now wanted to erase Paul’s existence.
The dokkaebi executor grinned, baring sharp fangs.
[Of all a dokkaebi’s powers, execution authority demands the greatest probability. Did you think you could use that authority for such a crude, contrived development and escape unscathed?]
[This can’t be. This can’t be happening!]

[Paul. You had a chance to end the scenario without using ‘execution authority’. And with a fresh development unlike anything seen before, at that. Why did you stop it? Your atrocities have put the Seoul Dome’s Bureau on emergency alert.]
[Th-that was······ No, wait a moment. I activated execution authority in accordance with the constellations’ wishes!]
Growing frantic, Paul looked around.
[C-constellations! Didn’t you agree with my development earlier?]
But the constellations gave no answer.
[······Constellations?]
The constellations’ indirect messages, so numerous before, were utterly silent at that moment.
[H-how could this······? Why?]
All the constellations who had supported his development had left the Korean Peninsula’s channels.
The Enforcement Division frowned.
[You fool. You didn’t even realize the constellations were gone?]
The many constellations who had egged him on and wanted me dead had deserted the Korean Peninsula’s channels en masse the moment the scenario’s ending turned into a ‘tearjerker’.
It was only natural.
After all, it would be strange to keep watching once a development they didn’t want appeared.
In fact, Bihyung’s channel had also lost nearly a third of its subscribing constellations.
And those who remained.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ glares at intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ looks at intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’ and snickers.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ mocks intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’.]
Every one of them was a constellation who had not agreed with the intermediate dokkaebi’s development.
[N-no. I cannot be annihilated like this. Executors!]
[Don’t worry. You will not be annihilated.]
[Th-then you mean······?]
For a brief moment, a glimmer of hope crossed Paul’s face.
The dokkaebi executor continued, as though mercilessly snuffing out that light.
[You will receive a punishment worse than annihilation. Because of you, our Bureau has been saddled with an enormous probability debt.]
The dokkaebi executor entered a [Restraint Code] into Paul’s body.
Paul had been in spirit form, but now his true body was forcibly summoned into the world. Trembling, intermediate dokkaebi Paul began to resist.
Stripped of his broadcast voice, he cried out in his own voice.
“Th-this is a conspiracy. This can’t be happening!”
Bihyung, standing beside him, spoke with a sneer.
[That’s why I told you we should end the scenario quickly.]
“Bihyung!”
Paul finally exploded. Flailing as he clutched at the restraint code, he pointed at Bihyung.
“Executor! Arrest him too. I have evidence that his channel violated the Star Stream’s rules!”
[Of course he will be coming with us too.]
Paul’s face brightened at those words. But in Korea, you had to hear someone out to the end, whether they were human or dokkaebi.
[Since dokkaebi Bihyung is the one who summoned us.]
“What do you······ Don’t tell me?”
The dokkaebi executor spoke.
[Bihyung is the dokkaebi who reported you.]
Bihyung gave a little wave to Paul, whose face alternated between red and blue. Wearing a peculiar smile, the dokkaebi executor continued.

[Dokkaebi Bihyung. A most excellent dokkaebi. Look at his humility, wearing only a scrap of sackcloth. Such integrity, disregarding everything else to devote himself to scenarios, is the very archetype of a streamer. Quite unlike you, a mere dokkaebi dressed in a designer suit.]
Bihyung looked embarrassed at those words.
He probably hadn’t known either. That his poverty would come in handy like this.
“N-no! That bastard Bihyung isn’t that sort of······!”
[Shut up.]
Bound by the restraint code, Paul let out a horrific scream.
The dokkaebi executor’s expression hardened as he continued.
[You have already been disciplined twice. This is your third time. You of all people should know what the third punishment is, shouldn’t you?]
“This, this is absurd! Do you think my superior will allow this? You’re making a mistake. If you lay a hand on me now······.”
[We’ll hear the rest of your nonsense at the Bureau.]
A shining portal opened in midair.
At last, the time had come to say goodbye to that intermediate dokkaebi.
I probably wouldn’t see him in any future scenarios.
His burning eyes glared at me.
The moment I met that gaze, a flame rose inside me.
[‘Fourth Wall’ trembles due to heightened emotions.]
The Shin Yoosung from the future, scattering as ashes.
If it hadn’t been for the intermediate dokkaebi, she might have been saved.
Although she could never have returned to her own round, she might have made this world her new round and lived alongside us as it changed.
But that intermediate dokkaebi had trampled even that final possibility.
That was why I spoke now.
“Hold on. Wait.”
He would receive a punishment equivalent to death, but I couldn’t be satisfied with that.
Startled by my words, my companions looked at me.
[······Did you just call us?]
Of course they would be surprised.
They couldn’t have expected a mere incarnation to stop the Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis.
After studying me quietly, the dokkaebi executor spoke.
[I see. You’re that incarnation called ‘Kim Dokja’, aren’t you?]
The other dokkaebi asked.
[You know him?]
[An incarnation who has recently become famous around here. One of the strongest on the peninsula, yet apparently he still hasn’t signed a constellation sponsorship contract.]
Watching them chatter as they pleased, I immediately spoke to Bihyung through [Dokkaebi Communication].
‘Bihyung. I’ll give you 100,000 coins.’
Bihyung, who had been following the dokkaebi executors, opened his eyes wide.
‘Upgrade me to a Platinum Member of the [Dokkaebi Bag].’
―Wait, why all of a sudden?
‘Just do it.’
―Damn it······.
Watching the executors approach, I hurried Bihyung along. With a sigh, he began manipulating something in midair.
[100000 coins have been spent.]
[Congratulations! You have become a Platinum Member of the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’!]
Normally, the upgrade came with spectacular celebratory fireworks and visual effects, but I asked Bihyung to skip them.
Unlike [Gold Member] status, which cost only 5000 coins to attain, [Platinum Member] status brought an entirely different level of treatment.
[Well, incarnation Kim Dokja. Why did you call us?]
The executors asked, still unaware of my upgrade. Unlike other dokkaebis, they were mountainous in size, and merely facing them made me tense.
That was hardly surprising. Though they had lost their Status and fallen far, some of them had originally been Historical-grade constellations.
I let out a light breath and spoke.
“I request a ‘Private Dokkaebi Audience (獨對)’.”
[What?]
Taken aback by my words, the dokkaebi executors looked at each other. Then came a snort of laughter, followed by a voice.
[Only Platinum Members or higher may request a ‘private audience’······. Could it be?]
“You guessed right. Check for yourselves.”
At that, the two dokkaebis looked at each other again. They checked several details through the system, then exclaimed in astonishment.
[It’s true.]
[How on earth did an incarnation become a Platinum Member······?]
“Now, I qualify, don’t I?”
After a moment’s hesitation, the dokkaebi executor nodded.
[Indeed. Which dokkaebi do you wish to have a ‘private audience’ with? Platinum status permits audiences with dokkaebis up to quasi-upper-grade, and as for scheduling an appointment······.]
“There’s no need to schedule one. You already have the one I want with you.”
I pointed at the dokkaebi I wanted.
“I want a private audience with intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’.”
At those words, the Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis turned to each other again.
How long did they remain like that? The two dokkaebis burst out laughing at the same time.
[Pfft. Bwahahahaha!]
[Interesting. Don’t tell me······.]
The quick-witted executors seemed to have caught on to something.
Some distance away, Paul was looking toward us with a bewildered expression.
[A private audience with prisoner dokkaebi ‘Paul’ is granted.]
[You have 20 minutes for your private audience.]
As though they had found an entertaining spectacle, the Enforcement Division readily granted my request.
I had known they would.
The ‘Enforcement Division’ didn’t like other streamers to begin with.
By their very origins, they were closer to ‘subscribing constellations’ than to ‘streamers’.
No sooner had they finished speaking than a small, transparent dome appeared around Paul and me.
A ‘private audience’ was originally a space for constellations and dokkaebis to meet in secret.
[Your private audience with intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’ begins.]
But a thing’s purpose could always change depending on who used it.
Outside the dome, I could see Bihyung saying something to the executors.
Suddenly trapped alone with me, Paul ground his teeth and bared his hostility.
“Why did you ask to see me? I suppose you want to gloat?”
The [Restraint Code] the dokkaebi executors had placed on him still shimmered over his body. As long as that code remained, Paul could use neither his dokkaebi authority nor any of his innate power.
In other words, the bastard standing before me was completely powerless.
“Stop bluffing. I know exactly what situation you’re in.”
Paul faltered and backed toward the edge of the dome. But a condescending smile still lingered on his lips.
“Haha, I see. I think I understand what vulgar thoughts you’re having. You want to avenge that slave, don’t you?”

“How laughable. Did you think I wouldn’t understand a lowly human’s desires? Very well, go ahead and try. I don’t know how you learned about ‘private audiences’, but this is a place where neither party can take the other’s life. No matter how much you struggle······!”
I charged straight at him and drove my fist into his face with all my strength.
A jet of blue blood burst from his nose. Still failing to grasp what was happening, he let out a belated scream and crumpled to the ground. I spoke.
“I can’t kill you, but I can hit you.”
“Gaaaaagh! How dare you······!”
“There, your true colors are finally showing. I was sick of hearing that disgusting politeness anyway.”
“Guh, guh-huurgh······.”
“First time you’ve felt pain like this, isn’t it? You’ve never been beaten like this in all your life as a dokkaebi, have you?”
“Heh, heh-heh. Heheheh······.”
Even as he spilled blood, Paul was still laughing.
“Y-you’ve just made a mistake. Th-this space has special rules in place for those who abuse ‘private audiences’, as you are doing.”
As though it had been waiting, a message sounded.
[You have injured a dokkaebi inside the ‘private audience space’.]
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
Dokkaebis really were an insufferable bunch.
To think they had even set up this sort of penalty in case a constellation lost its temper and attacked them. Their greed for coins had reached ridiculous heights.
But I had known about the penalty, so I merely shrugged.
Wiping away his blood, Paul laughed.
“Foolish human. You bring ruin upon yourself through anger. Go on, hit me as much as you please. With the coins a mere incarnation like you possesses······.”
“How much do you think I have?”
At that moment, Paul fell silent.
“Doesn’t it seem strange? How a mere incarnation like me became a ‘Platinum Member’?”
Watching his wavering gaze, I grinned at him.
“I have plenty of coins. I made a fortune thanks to you.”
As Paul turned white, I quietly cracked my knuckles.
All the goddamn scenarios I had endured flashed through my mind.
[Coins possessed: 205,902C]
I recalled my last glimpse of the dying Shin Yoosung.
Incidentally, among the things I had told her was this.
―I’ll make sure to beat that dokkaebi bastard within an inch of his life.
So this was the first promise I would keep.
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
My next punch shattered his nose.
I didn’t say things like, ‘This one is for so-and-so.’
Thwaaack!
After all, none of these blows could count as revenge for anyone.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“Aaaaagh! A-a lowly human dares······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“Y-you think you can do this to me and get away······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“I’ll kill you! I swear, I swear I’ll······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“W-wait! Just a moment! Sto······.”
As he curled up in terror, I stopped punching for the first time. For an instant, hope entered his eyes.
“Y-yes. A wise decision. There is nothing to be gained by doing this here······.”
Watching him hastily return to polite speech, I asked.
“Did you stop?”
“When Yoosung told you to stop, did you?”
I looked down at him quietly. He said nothing.
Instead, he looked once at me and once at the ground. Finally, he looked at the sky. As though the one he blamed for his predicament were up there.
“Th-this is meaningless! Doing this won’t bring your dead companion back to life!”
It wouldn’t bring my dead companion back to life. That was true.
But.
“It does mean something.”
I raised my fist at him again as his horns trembled.
“If I’d died. Shin Yoosung would have done this too.”
Thwaaack!
Flesh flew in a violent spray, and one of his fangs flew out and rolled across the ground.
“Lee Hyunsung would have too. So would Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung.”
My fist slammed into his abdomen and ruptured his internal organs.
“And probably······ even that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk······.”
My companions outside the dome were watching.

Shin Yoosung, her eyes red and her fists clenched. Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung were shouting something. Lee Hyunsung’s eyes were reddening, his face solemn, and Yoo Sangah watched me, biting her lip hard.
I looked at Yoo Joonghyuk last, then turned my gaze back to Paul.
“I-I exist outside the scenarios! You can’t earn coins by doing this! There’s nothing in it for you!”
Coins······.
Right. In the end, that was all you dokkaebis could think about.
Some stories became coins.
Some stories didn’t become coins.
“Maybe you’re right.”
No constellation had issued a bounty scenario, and no sub-scenario had told me to take him down.
But that was precisely why this act had meaning.
Because no one had told me to do it.
“I’m doing it because there’s nothing in it for me.”
“Wh-what?”
Ever since the world’s destruction began, coins had become the guiding principle behind all humans’ behavior.
People acted because the constellations gave them coins, and didn’t act because the constellations didn’t give them coins.
But sometimes humans acted without regard for any of that.
“You probably don’t understand, but humans are animals who find meaning in life through things like this.”
“Wh-what are you······ Aaaaagh!”
I raised my fist again and began beating him.
Thwaaack!
The punches that followed crushed his face, his ribs, his joints, one by one, with meticulous care.
There was no danger of killing him, so I didn’t hold back.
Every blow the best I could deliver.
Each time his skin split and his bones crumbled, something deep inside me burst apart too.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
The truth was, I knew.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
I knew perfectly well. No matter how much I beat him, this could not offer even the slightest consolation for Shin Yoosung’s death.
The dead Shin Yoosung would not witness this scene.
But even so, I kept my fists moving.
I beat him, and beat him again.
Thwaaack!
Just as Yoo Joonghyuk had.
Just as he had continued regressing until the very last moment, even when no one understood his cause.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
Eventually, the constellations’ messages sounded from the air.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is excited by a development unlike anything previously seen.]
[You have received 500 coins in sponsorship.]
I stopped punching for a moment and looked up at the sky.
Even a story like this became a scenario for the constellations.
“This time, I’m not acting.”
[The 500 coins received in sponsorship have been returned.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is greatly flustered.]
They could think of it as a free service.
Right now, I didn’t care.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ expresses interest in your actions.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is deeply moved by your actions.]
I began punching again.
Only the sound of the dokkaebi’s skin bursting and his intermittent groans rang out.
The constellations silently watched what I did.
No one gave me coins, but I could feel that they were watching me.
And sometimes, that alone was enough.
“U-uuurgh······ I was wrong. P-please spare me! P-please! Please!”
Unable to endure any more, Paul dragged his body, beaten to a pulp, to the edge of the dome and pounded on it.
The dome’s wall rang hollowly, but the Enforcement Division didn’t respond.
If anything, they seemed to welcome my bizarre behavior.
I couldn’t know for certain, but they were probably saying things like this.
「So they can make coins that way too.」
「Those goddamn streamer bastards.」
The Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis didn’t like streamers. Having evolved into dokkaebis from beings of alien form (異形), the executors were good at fighting, but had no talent for leading scenarios.
Before long, Paul’s body was utterly mangled. I grabbed the bloodied wreck of him by the collar.
By now, I could probably start asking what I wanted to know.
“Where is Shin Yoosung’s soul now?”
A soul that died as a component of a scenario could not escape the shackles of its contract, even in death.
But it was different when the contract itself had ceased to exist.
Intermediate dokkaebi Paul spoke only after taking dozens more blows.
[Th······ that. I-I don’t know either. B-because you borrowed the archangels’ power······ o-our contract with that bitch was destroyed······.]
Just as I’d thought.
The dokkaebis had received ‘Beast Lord Shin Yoosung’ from a demon, and during the transfer, the bonds of the contract had been joined through demonic power.
And those bonds had all been burned away by Uriel’s [Hell Flames Ignition].
In other words, Shin Yoosung’s soul had lost its anchor and was now drifting through the world.
[Y-you. Will never, get, your companion, back······ That bitch’s soul, will soon, enter, the labyrinth, of worldlines······.]
With those final words, Paul collapsed.
[The ‘Private Dokkaebi Audience’ has ended.]
The transparent dome vanished, and the Enforcement Division swaggered over, whistling.
[Well, he’s suffered something terrible before even being referred for disciplinary action.]
They glanced at me, then departed with cheerful smiles. Watching Bihyung hurry after them, I asked.
‘Did you pay the bribe?’
―Of course. But didn’t you spend too many coins?
‘I still have plenty left.’
Paul had taken exactly 124 blows before losing consciousness.
[Coins possessed: 143,902C]
Bihyung sighed and glanced at me.
―Once I enter the Bureau, we won’t be able to communicate for a while. I’ll leave the channel open, so stay out of trouble while I’m gone. Please.
As Bihyung earnestly urged me to behave, I privately thought this was a good thing. With him gone, no one would object to what I was about to do.
[Settlement of additional rewards is delayed due to a scenario error.]
With the main scenario’s administrator entirely absent, scenario developments would stall for a while. It would only be a day or two, but that was enough time for me.
Looking up at the dokkaebis disappearing through the portal, I recalled my last conversation with Shin Yoosung.
―Don’t worry. You won’t die.
―What do you mean?
―I’ll help you come back to life. I’ve done it twice myself, and it’s more manageable than you’d think.
In truth, I had intended to avoid using this method right through to the end.
After all, this plan required her to die ‘once’.
And there was no firm guarantee she could return to life.
―I don’t know how long it’ll take. But if you’ll wait for me, if you don’t give up, I’ll make sure to bring you back to life.
If Shin Yoosung’s soul fell into the ‘labyrinth of worldlines’, bringing her back to life would become almost impossible.
But that hadn’t happened yet.
If I could only retrieve her soul, she could surely live again.
The problem was ‘how’ to find that soul.
I turned to Yoo Sangah.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“Yes.”
Even if Shin Yoosung’s soul came from another worldline, all souls ultimately passed through the ‘afterlife’ to leave this world.
I thought of several constellations associated with the afterlife.
But all of them were either somewhere I dared not approach, or possessed a Status so high that my present self could never establish a connection with them.
There was, however, one I might be able to work something out with.
“Could you perhaps call the ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’?”
At my words, Yoo Sangah hesitated briefly, then nodded.
A little later, faint sparks flickered around her.
Because of the probability spent last time, this wasn’t a direct descent, but I could clearly tell that Ariadne was faintly present within Yoo Sangah.
I spoke.
“Olympus. I want to make a deal with you.”
The sparks around her grew violent.
Well, that was understandable, considering how badly our last meeting had gone.
But this time, I had to yield.
I took a short breath, then went straight to the point.
“Let me meet your King of the Underworld (冥王).”
Now it was time to keep my second promise.
I could tell immediately from Yoo Sangah’s expression what Olympus’s answer was. Only after watching her face turn red, then pale, then finally blue did I think I had brought it up too hastily.
“Um······ Dokja-ssi.”
What sort of vicious curses had she heard? Yoo Sangah looked at me and hesitated for a long time. I found myself feeling sorry.
“Could you tell me what your constellation sponsors said?”

Electricity crackled from Yoo Sangah’s body. Ariadne seemed to be throwing quite a fit. I waited a little for things to calm down. I hadn’t known our previous exchange of three questions and answers would have such far-reaching consequences.
At last, the sparks subsided, and Yoo Sangah spoke with a sigh in her voice.
“She says the ‘Father of the Rich Night’ isn’t someone she can just bring here······.”
Father of the Rich Night.
That was the modifier of ‘Hades, King of the Underworld’, one of Olympus’s three chief gods.
A constellation who was one of Olympus’s three chief gods, but whose permanent residence in the Underworld excluded him from the ‘Twelve Olympians’, the nebula’s great constellations.
Well, Hades’s Status might be too high for Ariadne, a mere Historical-grade constellation, to make contact with him.
For the moment, I expressed my thanks.
“Thank you, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“But Dokja-ssi, are you perhaps······.”
Clever as she was, Yoo Sangah would already have known that the ‘Father of the Rich Night’ was Hades.
She probably had some inkling of why I was seeking him too.
After all, the story of Orpheus, who went to the Underworld to bring his wife Eurydice back to life, was a famous myth even in Korea.
“······Is it possible?”
In principle, bringing the dead back to life was impossible.

I received a probability correction through the effect of ‘King of No Killing’, but in most cases there was no such correction. Shin Yoosung was no exception. If indiscriminate resurrection had been possible in the first place, Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn’t have needed to regress.
But if I could somehow get my hands on her soul······.
“I can’t explain the details right now. I’m sorry.”
I didn’t want to spell out all my future plans while every constellation was watching. This incident had increased the number of constellations who disliked me, too.
I had made my move. The other side would take the bait.
What mattered now was patience.
I turned to the companions around me and spoke.
“Shall we get things in order first?”

As though they had been waiting, my companions approached one by one. Lee Gilyoung, glancing at Shin Yoosung; Jung Heewon, supporting Lee Hyunsung; Lee Jihye, who had been standing apart with a slightly sulky expression.
A lower-grade dokkaebi’s voice sounded from the air.
[I am dokkaebi ‘Youngki’, temporarily assigned to handle reward settlement.]
Apparently a newcomer, the dokkaebi continued in a somewhat stiff voice.
[I will now settle the additional rewards for the fifth scenario.]
With all the higher-ranking dokkaebis gone, it seemed the unwanted work had been dumped on this one.
[You have received ‘Ellain Forest’s Vital Force’.]
Everyone caught one of the little fruits falling from the air.

[What you have just received is the most widely used recovery medicine in the ‘Star Stream’. Even if you have suffered serious injuries, eating it and going to sleep will allow you to recover quickly, so please eat it and get plenty of rest.]
I had never encountered such a polite dokkaebi before, and it almost made me uncomfortable. Looking at me and several others, the dokkaebi continued.
[Additional rewards for the main contributors will be distributed this evening. Thank you all for your efforts, and I wish you the best in the next scenario.]
The voice vanished, and I looked at my companions holding their fruits.

More characters I didn’t know would have died, and someone was probably dying even now. But we had survived. My companions looked as though they didn’t know whether to be grateful for that or to grieve.
At times like this, someone had to take the lead.
Looking at each of them in turn, I slowly spoke.
“You all worked hard.”
A moment in which nothing was decided would ultimately remain just that: a moment in which nothing was decided.
What was sad was sad, and what was happy was happy.
If you at least decided something, that moment would remain meaningful.
“You really worked hard.”
Relief slowly spread across my companions’ faces, as though my insignificant words were a reward in themselves.
They deserved it.
Only then did the corners of Lee Jihye’s mouth begin to twitch, and she was the first to speak.
“······You were seriously awesome back there, ajusshi. A tiny bit cooler than my master, even. I’ll give you that.”

That was because I'd only just gotten a sense of what ‘snake’ Persephone wanted.
I slowly nodded.
After the human presence vanished, darkness swept into the hall.
Left alone, Persephone quietly regarded the remaining feast, then spoke.
[Clear it away. It doesn't taste good.]
Hands emerged from the darkness and swiftly carried off the plates.
Persephone watched the food on the plates go straight into the trash. Sword Master, SSS-grade Hunter, 10-circle Archmage······.
Flavors she had tasted so often that she was sick of them.
The darkness in the air rippled, and a voice sounded.
―Persephone. Why did you do that?
It was a voice that sounded as though space itself were speaking.
[Oh, my shy husband finally speaks.]
―I asked why you did that.
[Hades, this is what you wanted.]
―I never wanted that.
Persephone stared steadily into that darkness before speaking.
[You rarely create incarnations. Yet you seemed particularly fond of that child. Was I mistaken?]
―Why did you think that?
[Because you didn't strike him dead the moment he came to the Underworld.]
The darkness was silent for a moment.
[You've always envied Zeus for having Heracles. So this time, I took the liberty of reading a little of my husband's heart.]
Looking down at her hand for a moment, Persephone clenched and unclenched her fist as she continued.
[Honestly, I was surprised. There were even constellations beyond what I could handle. To think such beings would follow a mere incarnation around······.]
With a crackle of static, a screen appeared in the darkness.
But perhaps the channel's signal was unstable, because the image didn't appear immediately.
The darkness gazed at the screen with lonely eyes, then spoke.
―Before long, signs of the days to come (後日) will appear.
The days to come. Hearing those words, Persephone spoke in a voice that mingled disbelief, doubt, and unease in equal measure.
[······Will those days really come?]
―Probably.
[But you'll still be by my side then, won't you?]
Hades did not answer. Instead, the comforting darkness held a gentle warmth as it carefully embraced her symbolic body. Feeling that darkness, Persephone spoke.
[I'm very eager to see what kind of story that child will show us.]
Where her gaze fell, the image of Kim Dokja could be seen, making his way through the darkness to leave the Underworld.
Kim Dokja, moving forward as he struggled to avoid looking back, even by accident.
Persephone smiled faintly, as though she found him endearing.
